dedupe_keys.name: anac brazil air transport statistics dados estatisticos do transporte aereo by flight stage and origin destination

description: Brazil's civil aviation agency ANAC publishes the monthly statistics that Brazilian and foreign airlines must report on their flights in Brazil: passengers (paid and free), cargo, mail, distance flown, flight hours, departures, seats and payload offered, revenue and available tonne-kilometres, and fuel consumed (Brazilian airlines only). Data come at two levels, the flight stage between take-off and landing and the origin-destination of passengers and cargo, broken down by airline and by nature of flight (domestic or international, scheduled, non-scheduled or non-revenue). Airlines report by the tenth day of the following month. The full series is online as open data on ANAC's file server, as one CSV file (about 360 MB) and JSON files for 2000 to 2010, 2011 to 2020 and 2021 to 2030, all refreshed on 26 September 2026, and is free to download. Coverage is national, airport by airport, since 2000. Caveats: figures are subject to revision and correction, and for foreign airlines load factors can exceed 100 per cent when split by airport because of how the demand variables are computed; the licence is not stated on the pages read. The series gives airport and route demand for air network flow models, capacity planning and scenario studies of airport disruption, and relates to OpenFlights and OurAirports catalogued here.
